analysis.title: Robert Half International Inc. (RHI): NDR highlights improving staffing and Protiviti trends, with minimal AI displacement currently
key_insights: GS hosted a non-deal roadshow with RHI CEO Keith Waddell and CFO Michael Buckley in San Francisco on 11/2 and came away incrementally more positive on the staffing recovery, the Protiviti recovery and AI positioning. The rating stays Sell.

Staffing volumes are near an inflection. Reported bill-rate growth of ~2.5% implies units fell about 1% in 3Q, an improvement from double-digit declines over prior quarters. The 3.6% mix-adjusted bill-rate increase overstates the volume decline because the adjusted measure normalizes for mix shifts such as faster growth in lower-rate markets like Brazil.

RHI has recovered more slowly than the staffing industry because 70%+ of its customers are SMBs, and enterprise demand typically leads SMB demand. SMBs have limited excess capacity after years of tight headcount management, which should create staffing need as demand improves.

Permanent placement is recovering faster than contract staffing, helped by low unemployment, talent scarcity and RHI's experienced recruiters. Perm fell ~45% peak to trough in the latest downturn versus ~65% after the Dot-Com and GFC cycles and ~30-35% for contract staffing. Management said perm is more volatile quarter to quarter, especially in 4Q, when year-end bonuses and holidays can delay placements.

RHI has seen no measurable AI displacement in its most exposed categories (accounting operations, customer service, technology support, help desk, PC technician). Existing automation (QuickBooks, Microsoft Dynamics) already covers routine accounting tasks, and SMB staffing models limit displacement because a 20% productivity gain in one task does not let a small company cut 20% of an employee who does several jobs.
GS says the absence of measurable AI displacement to date does not remove longer-term labor-demand risk as adoption broadens and companies redesign workflows.

Protiviti should accelerate in 4Q and stay elevated for at least one year, driven by contractor-heavy AML remediation projects and improving technology consulting demand. The projects were in sourcing and training in 3Q. Protiviti books no revenue during training because the work is priced per completed file, so billing should ramp in 4Q, approaching the target run rate by quarter-end without averaging it for the quarter.

More than 70% of the AML work is contractor-based, which supports margins through higher contractor mix and better utilization of full-time consultants kept after the 2Q cost actions. Risk and compliance is only ~20% of Protiviti. Technology consulting is the largest practice at ~35% and is improving as companies modernize legacy systems ahead of AI.

RHI says it kept enough recruiter and consultant capacity to return to prior peak operating margins, with more upside in a strong recovery. Full-Time Engagement Professionals fell to ~15-16% of contract revenue from the low-20% range and carry the highest contract gross margin in Talent Solutions.

RHI's differentiation is proprietary candidate performance data, brand, local distribution and AI-enabled matching (vector-based matching used for over a decade) and sales tools. The company argues this is harder for digital-only competitors and general-purpose models to copy.

RHI is keeping the dividend and returning essentially all FCF to shareholders. If FCF exceeds the dividend requirement in 2027, the excess goes to buybacks. Cash conversion may lag the recovery at first because higher revenue requires more receivables investment.

Macro swing factors: an end to current wars, lower energy prices, easing inflation and lower rate pressure would help hiring. Prolonged wars, higher energy costs, renewed inflation or higher rates would hurt. A broader recession, including an AI capex correction reaching labor demand through wealth effects, is the largest downside risk.

GS 12-month price target is $33 (26.3% downside from $44.77), based on 13.5x NTM+1YR EPS of $2.42, a slight discount to the staffing peer median NTM P/E of 14.0x to reflect AI disintermediation risk in white-collar staffing, offset by higher-margin perm and Protiviti mix. The target was raised from $29 (7/24/26 table entry) to $33 on 23-Oct-26.
The stock is up 70.9% over 12 months (55.0% relative to the S&P 500) and 65.7% over 6 months, per the report's price performance table.

market_movers.rationale: Sell reiterated after the NDR. The staffing recovery is gradual, SMB demand lags, and AI has not caused measurable displacement but remains a longer-term demand and valuation risk. Target implies 26.3% downside from $44.77.

sector_views.rationale: Staffing volumes are near an inflection and perm is leading the recovery, but the recovery is gradual and SMB demand lags. GS uses a peer median NTM P/E of 14.0x for the staffing group.

earnings_insights: RHI GS estimates: FY26E EPS $1.28 (vs FY25 reported $1.33, -3.2% y/y), FY27E EPS $1.98 (+54.2%), FY28E EPS $2.56 (+29.6%). These are GS estimates, not reported figures.

GS quarterly EPS: Sept-26 $0.49 (shown as P in the balance sheet exhibit, a GS model figure for the quarter already reported), Dec-26E $0.39, Mar-27E $0.33, Jun-27E $0.43. Dec-26E and later are GS estimates.
GS FY26E revenue $5,330.6mn (-0.9% y/y) and FY27E $5,546.2mn (+4.0%). Quarterly y/y growth in the model: Sept-26 +0.4%, Dec-26E +2.5%, Mar-27E +3.1%.
GS FY26E EBITDA $267.4mn, FY27E $354.7mn, FY28E $429.0mn. Adjusted EBITDA margin is 5.0% in FY26E, 6.4% in FY27E and 7.3% in FY28E (GS estimates).
Protiviti revenue in the GS model: Sept-26 +? y/y of -2.9%, Dec-26E +2.0%, FY27E +5.3%. Protiviti operating margin forecast is 5.8% in FY26E.
Dividend per share GS estimate $2.38 in FY26E and $2.60 in FY27E, with payout ratio of 185.5% in FY26E falling to 131.4% in FY27E. FCF is $230.6mn in FY26E versus dividends paid of $239.3mn.
risk_factors: Gradual staffing recovery and lagging SMB demand.
Longer-term AI disintermediation of white-collar staffing roles and workflow redesign, even though no measurable displacement has occurred so far.
Perm revenue volatility, particularly in 4Q from year-end bonus timing and holiday schedules.
Prolonged wars, materially higher energy costs, renewed inflation or meaningfully higher interest rates would hurt employer confidence and hiring.
A broader recession, including an AI capital-spending correction that reaches labor demand through equity-market and wealth effects.
Cash conversion may lag the recovery because higher revenue requires receivables investment.
Dividend absorbs nearly all of reduced FCF, leaving limited room for buybacks until FCF recovers.
geopolitical: The report says an end to the current wars would help employer confidence and hiring, and prolonged wars would pose the opposite risk. It does not name specific conflicts.

tension_points.bull_case: Staffing units fell only ~1% in 3Q versus double-digit declines before, perm is leading, Protiviti AML billing starts in 4Q for at least a year, and RHI retained capacity to return to prior peak margins. No measurable AI displacement so far.
tension_points.bear_case: The recovery is still gradual, SMB demand lags, and AI remains a longer-term source of demand and valuation uncertainty. The dividend absorbs nearly all reduced FCF, and a recession or AI capex correction is the largest downside risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bear case weakens if staffing volumes turn positive and Protiviti AML billing ramps as expected in 4Q, and if FCF exceeds the dividend in 2027 enabling buybacks.
